tldr: At the headline layer, the US-Saudi F-35 sale is overwhelmingly framed as a dollar-value transaction: nine of eleven country buckets lead with the $24.3 billion figure or a near equivalent, making ECONOMIC the dominant advertised frame. Two notable exceptions break from this consensus: Israel's Jerusalem Post pivots entirely to a compensation narrative ('Israel will seek new weapons systems from US as compensation'), while Southeast Asia's Malay Mail embeds the sale in active warfare ('amid Iran war'). France's AFP uniquely names the Trump administration as the approving actor, a political attribution absent from every other headline.

bottom_line: At the headline layer, the US-Saudi F-35 deal reads primarily as a major dollar-value transaction: most outlets worldwide foreground the $24.3 billion figure and nothing else. The Israeli and Southeast Asian press alone crack the economic shell — Jerusalem Post frames it as an Israeli compensation story, Malay Mail embeds it in the live Iran war — divergences entirely suppressed by the neutral headlines from Pakistan, Russia, and Canada.
